title: Transit fare strategy and city water plans
subtitle: Water and stormwater master plans, annual water report, delegation of authority by-law, and student and senior transit passes.
overview: The committee's main item was the Transit Fare Strategy. It recommended making Kids Ride Free (ages 12 and under) permanent and approving a fare capping program, under which riders pay per trip until they reach the cost of a monthly pass and then ride free for the month {{vote:m5}}. It also asked staff to report back before the 2024-2027 budget on making passes more accessible for high school students and seniors {{vote:m6}}.

The committee also recommended approving the Water and Wastewater Servicing Master Plan {{vote:m2}} and the Stormwater Management Master Plan {{vote:m4}}. Their costs go to the City's rate models and multi-year budget process. It approved the 2022 Water Services Annual Report {{vote:m3}}. Staff said the provincial audit found no risks in the drinking water system.

The committee further recommended an updated Delegation of Authority By-law, which repeals two older by-laws {{vote:m1}}. These are recommendations. Council must still adopt them. Residents can expect higher transit fares and new fare options, along with more public engagement as stormwater projects reach the design stage.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended making Kids Ride Free permanent, approving the Fare Capping Loyalty program, and delegating staff to proceed with the remaining strategy initiatives, with budget impacts going to the 2024-2027 multi-year budget.

decisions.item: Transit passes for students and seniors
decisions.detail: The committee recommended directing staff to report back before the 2024-2027 budget on making transit passes more accessible for high school students and seniors, including best practices from comparator municipalities.

decisions.item: Water and Wastewater Servicing Master Plan
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the plan, filing a Municipal Class Environmental Assessment Notice of Completion, and referring its financial information to the water and wastewater rate models and long-range financial plans.
The committee recommended approving the plan, filing the Notice of Completion, and referring its financial implications to the multi-year budget process.
The committee recommended approving the 2022 Water Services Annual Report and Summary Report.
The committee recommended approving the revised Delegation of Authority By-law and repealing the 2013 Delegation of Authority and Execution of Documents by-laws.

debate: On stormwater, one councillor asked why a surface pond was proposed for a particular park. Staff said surface facilities generally cost less to build and maintain and provide habitat. They said detailed design and community consultation come later, when each project is resourced.

Councillors asked how residents can find out about projects planned for their parks. They said residents struggled to find information across several plans. Staff agreed to take the concern back and to coordinate with the parks and recreation master plan.

Councillors raised safety and environmental questions about stormwater ponds, including winter ice use, wildlife habitat and heritage areas. Staff said the ponds are infrastructure, not recreation facilities, and that the public is discouraged from using them.

On transit, a delegate from the Transit Advisory Committee supported Kids Ride Free as a way to build lifelong ridership. The delegate said the committee had not had a full review before the meeting but raised no significant concerns about fare capping.

Councillors questioned the 90-minute transfer window, the location of self-serve fare terminals and a possible capital surcharge on fares. Staff said transfer complaints are rare and agreed to review the window in a year. They said a surcharge would need a broader review through the budget process.
